selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: At the time of Maghrib prayer, what kind of Lord does the human spirit turn toward?
questions.answer: It turns toward Allah, the Everlasting Lord who never dies and remains forever.

questions.question: How are worldly things described in this part?
questions.answer: They are described as passing away and not lasting.

questions.question: What is the first big action the worshipper takes toward Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: He turns away from temporary things and turns toward Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper begin with praise?
questions.answer: Because Allah deserves thanks and honor for His perfect qualities and mercy.

questions.question: What does asking only Allah for help teach a Muslim student about daily life?
questions.answer: It teaches him to depend on Allah first and not treat others as equal to Him.

questions.question: What belief about Allah’s position is shown by worshipping Him alone?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah alone is the Lord, God, and Sovereign without any partner.

questions.question: What does prostration show in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows love, worship, humility, and leaving everything besides Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the worshipper’s feelings in prostration?
questions.answer: He feels wonder, love, and deep humility.

questions.question: What does the final glorification in prostration say about Allah?
questions.answer: It says that Allah is the Most High and far above every fault or decline.

questions.question: What is the central message of this whole passage about prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer turns the heart away from the fading world and toward Allah, who alone is perfect and everlasting.

questions.question: What happens in the human spirit at Maghrib according to the passage?
questions.answer: It faces Allah, who is everlasting, because the spirit longs for what is eternal.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the things of this world?
questions.answer: They change, fade, and cannot be depended on forever.

questions.question: What does saying “Allah is the Greatest” help the worshipper do?
questions.answer: It helps him break attachment to temporary things.

questions.question: What three qualities of Allah are highlighted when He is praised in this passage?
questions.answer: His perfect greatness, unmatched beauty, and endless mercy.

questions.question: What is being praised in Allah according to the passage?
questions.answer: His perfection, His unique beauty, and His great mercy.

questions.question: What is the meaning of glorifying Allah while bowing?
questions.answer: It means declaring that Allah is عظیم, perfect, and far above every weakness or fault.

questions.question: During prostration, what does the worshipper leave behind?
questions.answer: He leaves behind everything other than Allah.

questions.question: What does the worshipper discover when he abandons all else and turns to Allah?
questions.answer: He discovers Allah’s mercy and finds Him as the Compassionate Eternal Lord.

questions.question: What does the worshipper declare about Allah at the end of prostration?
questions.answer: He declares that Allah is the Most High and completely free from every flaw.

questions.question: If a student summarized this passage in one sentence, what would be a good summary?
questions.answer: Maghrib prayer teaches us to leave the love of fading things and worship Allah alone with praise, humility, and love.

questions.question: At Maghrib, why is the spirit especially ready to turn to Allah?
questions.answer: Because the spirit wants lasting beauty, and only Allah is truly everlasting.

questions.question: Who is the only One in the passage that truly remains forever?
questions.answer: Allah is the only One who truly remains forever.

questions.question: What does standing before Allah show about the worshipper?
questions.answer: It shows respect, service, and readiness to worship.

questions.question: After turning to Allah, what does the worshipper do first in worship?
questions.answer: He stands before Allah and praises Him.
